text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Skopje press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
- Macedonian Prime Minister Branko Crvenkovski proposed in principle compensatin of deposits to TAT savers but with no interest and in the form of foreign currency bonds.
- Crvenkovski will participate at the Forum Cran Montana '97 in Switzerland. He is expected to address the plenary session on Thursday on security in south-east Europe.

- Simon Lann, secretary general of NATO assembly, said that alliance cannot resolve Macedonian problems but added that NATO was seriously considering Macedonian offer for the use of Krivolak as a military training range.
- The average wage in April in Macedonia stood at 9,016 denars or some 333 German marks.
- Macedonia to open its embassy in Berlin on July 1.

- The Macedonian Constitutional Court handed down a temporary ruling for the removal of Albanian flag in front of Tetovo municipality building. But municipal authorities said they would not execute their ruling and would wait for the parliament decision on the issue.
- Macedonian company OHIS and U.S. Texaco signed an agreement on technical cooperation in Skopje on Wednesday. OHIS is to supply high concentrated chemicals for engine cooling.

- East-west and north-south corridors that meet in Macedonia have received priority in construction and international financial support, said Tito Petkovski, Macedonian parliament speaker upon his arrival from the Pan European conference on transportation.
- Macedonian Army experts demand urgent dislocation of the unexploded artillery shells from the Pestani beach in Ohrid remained there since World War One.
- Ministry of interior discovered a number of irregularities in financial operations of former high officials in the capital of Skopje. -- Mircela Casule, Skopje newsroom +389 91 201 196
